Do you think any species capable of interstellar travel would have abandoned their physical bodies a long time ago?

Yes. That seems likely to me. In fact, I strongly suspect that this may be a prospect in our own near-term space development, long before we realize any interstellar capability. The safest and most cost-efficient form of space travel is telecommunications. The safest and most cost-efficient way of operating in the space environment is by use of telerobots. The most cost-efficient, easily-deployed, adaptable, and practical form of 'settlement' in space is a data center.

Despite the hype about manned space travel and colonization today, the future really doesn't look that good for manned spacecraft and suited astronauts. They're not needed. We may never actually need a manned spaceflight capability all that much larger in scale than today's Soyuz-style systems. The proposed manned missions to Mars getting so much attention right now may, if they even happen, be the last hurrah for man-in-space. Very soon, most of the activity we do in near-Earth space will be done like this by technicians sitting in offices on Earth. Artificial intelligence will be applied to extend the reach of this kind of activity, compensating for telecommunications latency at greater distances through local machine intelligence, letting those technicians sitting in their offices easily manage vast projects in deep space. When we achieve functional Artificial General Intelligence (which now is expected within no more than few decades), it will assume the leading role in all space activity by virtue of economy. As long as doing things in space demands taxpayer money or corporate capital, one is compelled to do them in the absolute cheapest way. If they're more expensive, you can't use astronauts just because you think humans should be in space. NASA has avoided that as long as it could by suppressing certain space robotics development and using circular reasoning to justify a need for humans. It can't do that anymore. There are too many competing players in the game now and the 'bottom line' will out. No matter what fanciful spacecraft technology we invent in the future, manned spaceflight will never be able to compete with minds that can travel across space by wireless telecom. So either people will form large intentional communities to pool their resources to go live in space for sake of a lifestyle there, regardless of the expense or practicality, or they will have to figure out how to join those machine intelligences and travel in space by telecom like they do.

So the first true settler on Mars may be Watson and if you want to go live that supposedly adventurous life in space, you may have to leave the 'wetware' behind on Earth. The common method of space travel for organic human beings may be going to sleep in a pod like in a Japanese Capsule Hotel where your body gets stored and waking up in a VR habitat on a data center somewhere in space. Traveling to other star systems may be a process of having your mind and the blueprint for your body transmitted across space by an enormous solar-pumped telecom laser to be reconstituted from local materials at a distant machine-built settlement.
